title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized filters. No raw SQL or string interpolation into queries is present anywhere in the diff.

SSFStreamViewSet is upgraded from ReadOnlyModelViewSet to include DestroyModelMixin. The viewset has no explicit permission_classes or ownership check visible in the diff. The queryset is Stream.objects.all() with no filtering by authenticated user or provider ownership. Any authenticated user who can reach this endpoint may be able to delete any stream by UUID (IDOR/missing authz). Whether adequate permission classes are inherited from a base class or router configuration cannot be confirmed from this diff alone, but the lack of explicit authorization on the newly added destroy action is a concern.

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit permission_classes (e.g., IsAuthenticated plus an ownership/admin check) to SSFStreamViewSet, and restrict the queryset to streams belonging to providers the requesting user is authorized to manage. Alternatively, verify that the router or a parent mixin enforces this.
